semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: 'Impact evaluation' generally includes the assessment of effects stemming from various sources, including pandemics like COVID-19, which aligns with 'covid-19 impact studies'.

parent_domains.justification: This is a broader field encompassing the study of disease patterns, causes, and effects in populations which COVID-19 studies fit into.
A very broad field covering all epidemiological research, which certainly includes COVID-19 impact studies.
Involves assessing the effects of various phenomena, such as a pandemic, on society or specific fields.
This field concerns health issues and concerns that transcend boundaries, like COVID-19, affecting populations worldwide.

closest_parent_domain.justification: COVID-19 impact studies specifically reside under this field as it directly aligns with the investigation of disease propagation and outcomes associated with infectious diseases.

child_domains.justification: Part of the broader COVID-19 impact evaluation, focusing specifically on social and economic dimensions.
Deals specifically with how societies adapt and the impacts felt from large scale events like pandemics, under the COVID-19 impact umbrella.

closest_child_domain.justification: This domain focuses specifically on one of the main areas of study within COVID-19 impact studies - how the pandemic has affected economies and social structures broadly.

sibling_domains.justification: Aims at observing and understanding the progression of infectious diseases, related closely to impact studies but from a monitoring perspective.
Deals with the use of intervention data, which complements impact studies with insights from data derived from interventions.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Closely aligned with COVID-19 impact studies as it involves tracking and analyzing data to monitor the spread and impact of the disease.

unrelated_domains.justification: Focuses more on biological systems other than direct studies on diseases or pandemics like COVID-19.
Involves studying impacts specifically related to climate change, not directly related to diseases.
Specifically pertains to greenhouse gas emissions, irrelevant to infectious diseases.
Focuses on the immune system in general, without specific relation to pandemic impact.
More related to the study of the immune response to viruses rather than direct pandemic impacts.
Studies viral genetic makeup which doesn’t directly relate to impact evaluation.
Focuses on diseases with low prevalence rather than the wide-reaching impacts of a pandemic like COVID-19.
Centered on vaccine development and effects, not on broader societal or epidemiological impacts.
While related to global health, this field focuses more on specific health policies and programs rather than broad impacts.
This field studies gene-disease associations, which doesn’t directly tie into impact analysis of pandemics.
